final_answer: Ice floats on water because of its unique molecular structure. When water freezes, the molecules arrange themselves into a hexagonal lattice held together by hydrogen bonds. This structure creates more open space between the molecules compared to liquid water, making ice less dense. Since ice is less dense than liquid water, it floats on top of it.
